text:
arjun: quick thread to capture ideas after yesterday's long-run frag spike. reproducer in /tmp/frag-heavy.tar.gz
mira: saw the same in staging. fragmentation climbs slowly but steady under mixed tiny alloc + pinned embeddings.
kevin: pattern looks like: many ~3-8KB allocations, then a few long-lived pinned ranges that block coalescing. slab internal slack increases.
sana: initial thought: instead of global compaction waves, try tokenized compaction quotas per-tenant. each tenant gets X compact-tokens per epoch to spend on compaction work.
arjun: token idea is interesting. it bounds compaction CPU and prevents thundering herd across tenants. how to compute X? proportional to tenant allocation footprint or historical frag_rate?
mira: compute base tokens = footprint_mb / K, then add frag_delta bonus if frag_ratio increases above threshold. also allow emergency tokens when host-level frag exceeds global watermark.
kevin: implementation sketch:
- allocator maintains per-tenant token_bucket (capacity, refill_rate)
- compact_hint(tenant, urgency) consumes tokens; urgency=now drains bucket (if empty, returns false)
- background compaction drains slowly via refill
- allocator emits backpressure when total token consumption rate > host cap

sana: nice. also propose a "compact_taint" bit for slabs: a slab marked tainted will be deprioritized for allocation until compacted or until taint expires. helps avoid scattering new tiny allocs into high-frag slabs.
arjun: good call. taint TTL should be conservative so we don't starve pools. maybe exponential backoff per-slab if repeated compaction attempts fail.
mira: rewarm tradeoffs: aggressive rewarm increases bandwidth & CPU. we should add a tiny rewarm sampler: on first miss after compaction, schedule a small async prefetch for neighbor cache-lines/pages, bounded by a per-tenant rewarm_budget. track rewarm_hits to tune budget.
kevin: so we have two budgets now: compaction tokens + rewarm tokens. we need observability: per-tenant frag_ratio, token_bucket_level, compact_cycles, rewarm_attempts, rewarm_hits, slab_taint_count.
sana: about integration: who owns tokens? allocator obviously for compaction tokens. rewarm tokens probably runtime-level because it knows prefix cache heuristics. they can be advertised via a simple API: runtime.request_rewarm(tenant, slab_id, budget).
arjun: admission controller should subscribe to allocator backpressure metrics and throttle noisy tenants. this prevents eviction storms when compaction ramps.
mira: corner case: pinned ranges inside a slab prevent compaction for that slab. allocator should expose slab_pinned_fraction so policy can skip compaction attempts on those slabs and reassign tokens elsewhere.
kevin: ops suggestion: add a debug endpoint that lists top N slabs by frag_gain if compacted. that makes it easy to choose which slabs to compact first in experiments.
sana: perf experiment plan:
1) simulate 100 tenants with mixed tiny alloc & pinned long-lived ranges. baseline: global compaction every 30s.
2) tokenized compaction + slab_taint + rewarm sampler. measure CPU, bandwidth, frag_ratio, tail latency.
3) stress emergency-token refill path under enforced global watermark.

compaction-bot: snapshot saved: tokenized-compact-probe by arjun at 1732550123
arjun: I'll open RFC draft with API sketches: allocator.token_bucket, allocator.compact_hint, runtime.request_rewarm, slab metadata (taint, pinned_fraction). keep API minimal to start.
mira: I'll write the sim harness and post graphs. aiming to land canary on staging in 10 days if sim looks good.
kevin: cool. small note: ensure compaction work is preemptible and yields frequently so it doesn't harm inference p99. add CPU budget guard in compaction worker.
sana: agreed. also add metric for compaction_yield_count per-cycle.
arjun: ok team, will follow up with RFC link and a checklist for metrics + canary rollout steps. thanks!
